Resolves #18646

🌿 The reclaim route had witnesses who read too early and rigs nobody committed; now one arm reads after the transit, on the instance, and a pane that came home as anything but itself has nowhere left to hide.

`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationReclaimEmbodimentNL.spec.mjs` — three arms on the real Workstation through the `neuralLink` fixture, a sibling-file lift of `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` (same helpers, same pop-out path). Arm 1 pops `feed` out through the focus-gated pop-out action into a real vessel, presses the real `Reset to default`, and polls until the SAME live pane (identity through `getPaneIdentity`) is embodied in the root — `windowId` flipped, `mounted`, in the root DOM, gone from the vessel's, its tab in the home strip — then presses the real `Undo` and polls until the same instance is embodied in the vessel again. Arm 2 shortens `reconnectLeaseMs` through the live manager, reads the Group's slot at the `popup` event — the reservation, generation 0 and no window — closes the vessel, then polls the slot until a read is no longer that reservation: it must be `null`, no sooner than one lease after the click that reserved it, so the route is the never-bound expiry and nothing else; it then asserts the pane parked (`mounted: false`) and not destroyed with its identity unchanged, clicks `Show <vessel> here`, and polls until the same instance is embodied in the root. Arm 3 is the control for that witness: the vessel connects (the slot reads generation 1 with the popup's window), closes through `window.close()`, the slot reads generation 1 with no window, and the same poll returns that released record instead of `null` — the pane parks identically, which is why the slot and not the pane names the route. Every embodiment read is a poll after the transit; no assertion reads the document alone.

Evidence: L3 (the real Workstation with a real vessel window, driven through the production buttons and read through the Neural Link, locally with the runtime root) → L3 required (embodiment across real window realms is not observable in the unit tier). Residual: none — the spec is Brain-dependent (`testIgnore` without `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`) and workstation specs sit outside the CI e2e-engine tier (`buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`, GPU), so no CI coverage is claimed and the receipts below are the coverage.

| AC-2 | arm "a vessel that never connected keeps its retained pane past the lease …": green in runs 3–6; `reconnectLeaseMs` 3000 read back before the vessel opens; the slot reads `{generation: 0, windowId: null}` at the popup event, before the close; the poll leaves the reservation only at `null`, after ≥ 1 reservation read and ≥ 2900 ms since the click; embodiment `{mounted: false, isDestroyed: false}`; `Show <vessel> here` re-trees to `{root window · mounted, rootDom 1}` with the identity unchanged |
| AC-3 | M-B — `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` checked out from `07e4e113e8^` (the pre-#18635 engine): arm 2 red exactly on "the retained pane is parked, not destroyed" with `{isDestroyed: true, mounted: null, windowId: null}`. M-C — `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs#resolvePane` rebuilding the pane on every resolution: arm 1 red at "the vessel renders the live pane", before Reset. Both restored with `git checkout`. Route control — arm 3: bound `{generation: 1, windowId: <popup>}`, released `{generation: 1, windowId: null}`, the never-bound poll returns `{left: {generation: 1, windowId: null}, reservedReads: 0}`, the pane parks with the same identity, the slot leaves ≥ 2900 ms after the release |
| AC-4 | this body's `Evidence:` line, and the spec's header comment carrying the runtime-root requirement, the zero-tests-selected trap and the two lifecycle routes |

## Deltas from ticket
- Review R1 (Euclid): arm 2 now witnesses the route it claims — the reservation before the close, the untouched reservation on every read until the slot leaves, the lease measured from the click — and arm 3 shows the same instrument refusing the connected-then-closed route. No engine change.
- Two instrument corrections from the first run, recorded as Avoided Traps on #18646: `isDestroyed` reads `undefined` on a live pane through the Neural Link (normalised to `=== true`), and the tear-out commit is asynchronous to the `popup` event (the document holders are polled).
- A third, from the control's first run: Playwright's `page.close()` never dispatches `beforeunload`, and the disconnect rides on `main/DomEvents.mjs#onBeforeUnload` → `worker/Base#fire('disconnect')` → `Transaction#onWindowDisconnect`, so a vessel closed that way keeps its binding for good — `{generation: 1, windowId: <popup>}` for the whole 20 s poll. `window.close()` from inside the page is the real close. This is #18621's sighting 2 with its mechanism; recorded there.

- Positive controls as in AC-3, each run as the single arm it targets; the mutated engine and app files restored byte-for-byte.

### 📋 Required Actions

- [ ] **R1 [P2] — Witness never-bound expiry before asserting its outcome.** Arm 2's first binding assertion is already `getBinding(...) === null`; it observes neither the reserved generation nor a matching expiry. `popOut` awaits `button.click()` before returning the popup, and the popup event is emitted after its initial response starts loading, so closing at that point is not a never-bound witness. On this head, `Transaction.getBinding` exposes generation and windowId; reserve begins at generation 0, while a released bound generation is different. `NativeLifecycle.onLeaseExpired` selects an unconnected admission, whereas `onRelease` can independently retain a parked pane. Record the intended reservation/never-bound generation and its expiry, and ensure a deliberately connected-then-closed control is refused by that precondition. Keep the current pane/DOM/re-tree assertions and the existing mutation controls. The reported M-B run is useful evidence for that sample; the committed arm also needs to identify which lifecycle path it exercised.

This is an instrument requirement, not a claim that the product failed in this review. No additional engine change is requested. Source anchors: the new spec's arm 2; `src/manager/Transaction.mjs:480,833`; `src/manager/transaction/NativeLifecycle.mjs:302,332`.
